question: What is the main use of a urinal in the ward?

options.A: To collect stool samples from patients with gastrointestinal bleeding
options.B: To measure precise fluid intake during intravenous therapy
options.C: To collect urine from male patients who cannot walk to the bathroom
options.D: To replace indwelling urinary catheters in surgical patients permanently

explanation: Urinals are shaped specially for male anatomy so patients who are stuck in bed can pass urine easily without fuss. You will see these all the time on the medical-surgical wards! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h3)

question: A client looks very scared about going to the general hospital to remove a contraceptive implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Cancel the referral and send the client home without protection
options.B: Scold the client for being afraid of a minor procedure
options.C: Tell her that hospitals are terrifying places and she must just endure it
options.D: Listen to her concerns, explain the procedure simply, and reassure her

explanation: Fear is completely normal. Sitting down to listen and breaking down what will happen turns anxiety into confidence. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the essential clean delivery practices?

options.A: Clean cutting instrument for the cord
options.B: Clean surgical face mask for every visitor
options.C: Clean surface for the mother to deliver on
options.D: Clean hands of the birth attendant

explanation: The core clean delivery practices focus on hands, delivery surface, perineum, cord cutting tools, and cord ties rather than visitor masks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h6)

question: What should a nurse do when faced with an unclear or ambiguous prescription order?

options.A: Hold the drug for the entire day without telling anyone
options.B: Administer a standard average dose based on common practice
options.C: Ask a junior student nurse to guess what the doctor meant
options.D: Contact the prescriber immediately to clarify the exact instruction

explanation: Guessing an unclear order puts the patient at extreme risk; the prescribing clinician must always clarify ambiguous instructions. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is feeding through the gut (enteral nutrition) usually preferred over drips (parenteral nutrition) for surgical patients?

options.A: It preserves gut immune function and carries fewer infectious risks
options.B: It is absorbed much faster than intravenous fluids
options.C: It bypasses the digestive system entirely
options.D: It can be administered without any medical equipment

explanation: You got it! Using the natural digestive tract keeps the gut healthy and avoids the high infection risks that come with central lines. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h5)

question: Why is teaching patients how to read food labels so important on a low-fat diet?

options.A: Processed foods often contain hidden fats that are not obvious by appearance.
options.B: Labels help the patient calculate the exact cost of groceries.
options.C: Reading labels is a legal requirement for hospital discharge.
options.D: Nutrition labels tell the patient exactly when to take their medications.

explanation: Many packaged snacks hide extra fats where you least expect them. Reading labels helps patients spot those sneaky lipids! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h7)

question: Parenteral nutrition delivers concentrated calories and nutrients directly into which part of the body?

options.A: The muscular tissue of the upper thigh
options.B: The bloodstream through a central venous catheter
options.C: The stomach cavity through a percutaneous tube
options.D: The small intestine through a nasal tube

explanation: Parenteral nutrition bypasses the gut completely and sends nutrients straight into the bloodstream via a central line. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of demographic data?

options.A: Common cultural beliefs about healing
options.B: The number of available hospital beds
options.C: The pH level of the local drinking water
options.D: Age distribution and population size

explanation: Demographics focus on the statistical characteristics of human populations, such as age, size, and sex distribution. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h2)

question: A confused patient arrives at the emergency ward. What is one of the quickest bedside checks you should do?

options.A: A random blood glucose check
options.B: A twenty-four-hour urine collection
options.C: A complete neurological reflex test
options.D: A fasting lipid profile test

explanation: Always check blood sugar when a patient's mental status changes. It takes seconds to rule out severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, which can look just like confusion! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T19#GNS222_U2_T19_h2)

question: Why is it unhelpful to just write off a family planning defaulter as simply 'uncooperative'?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never return to the facility
options.B: It breaks hospital regulations regarding patient confidentiality
options.C: It automatically makes the client pregnant within a week
options.D: It ignores practical barriers and personal reasons driving the missed appointment

explanation: People miss appointments for real reasons—like side effects, transport costs, or busy schedules. Looking past the label helps us solve the actual problem together. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h1)

question: What vital sign must a nurse always check before a client starts taking combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: Oxygen saturation
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Temperature
options.D: Blood pressure

explanation: Always check the BP! Estrogen can push blood pressure up, so we need a safe baseline reading before handing out that first prescription. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h4)

question: Which set of clinical signs points straight to hypothyroidism?

options.A: Weight loss, heat intolerance, and rapid pulse
options.B: Severe hypertension, sweating, and tremors
options.C: Extreme thirst, frequent urination, and high sugar
options.D: Weight gain, cold intolerance, and sluggishness

explanation: When thyroid hormones drop, your body's engine slows way down. You feel cold, tired, and your metabolism drops, leading to weight gain. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h4)

question: What does milking a drainage tube involve?

options.A: Disconnecting the drainage bag completely and washing the inside with soap
options.B: Injecting large volumes of sterile water upward into the wound site
options.C: Twisting the tube tightly until the fluid stops flowing completely
options.D: Gently squeezing and releasing the tubing downward to push clots along

explanation: Milking is a gentle technique used to clear minor blockages by compressing the tubing progressively toward the collection container. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h3)

question: What main factor sets gender-based violence apart from other forms of violence?

options.A: It is directed against someone based on gender roles and inequalities
options.B: It only occurs within marriage and domestic settings
options.C: It is exclusively perpetrated by adult males against adult females
options.D: It involves physical assault without any psychological harm

explanation: You've got this! GBV stems from unequal power balances and societal expectations tied to gender. Recognizing this helps us look beyond just the physical acts. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T8#GNS312_U4_T8_h1)

question: When cleaning a hospital ward, why should you always clean from high areas to low areas, and clean zones to dirty zones?

options.A: To ensure that heavy cleaning buckets stay balanced on wheeled carts
options.B: To prevent dirt and pathogens from falling onto already cleaned surfaces
options.C: To reduce the total amount of chemical spray needed for the room
options.D: To speed up the chemical evaporation rate across large ward floors

explanation: Working top-to-bottom stops gravity from dropping dust and germs right back onto the spots you just finished cleaning! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h7)

question: What is another name for the sympathetic division based on where its nerves leave the spinal cord?

options.A: Thoracolumbar division
options.B: Cervicothoracic division
options.C: Lumbosacral division
options.D: Craniosacral division

explanation: Sympathetic preganglionic neurons emerge from the thoracic and upper lumbar regions of the spinal cord, giving it the thoracolumbar label. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h4)

question: What is the final goal of the complement cascade when attacking a bacterium?

options.A: Thickening of the local epithelial basement membrane
options.B: Production of specific IgE antibodies against the bacterial wall
options.C: Maturation of naive T-cells into active helper cells
options.D: Formation of a membrane attack complex that lyses the cell

explanation: You got it! The complement system builds a 'membrane attack complex' that drills holes in the germ until it bursts (lyses). [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main point of using data storytelling in healthcare?

options.A: To increase the daily paperwork burden for floor nurses
options.B: To hide negative hospital audit scores from the public
options.C: To connect numbers with patient care to drive action
options.D: To replace verbal nursing handover reports completely

explanation: You got this! Data storytelling turns boring stats into real human stories that help staff and leaders take action to improve care. Keep it up! [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do body cells swell and break open during the final stages of dying?

options.A: Sodium and water rush in because cell pumps stop working
options.B: Lactic acid builds up inside blood vessels
options.C: White blood cells attack healthy tissues
options.D: Extra glucose pulls water into the cells

explanation: Without ATP, the tiny pumps that keep sodium out of cells stop working. Sodium stays inside, brings water with it, and causes the cell to swell. Great thinking! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of sharing (disseminating) nursing research?

options.A: Filing clinical documents away safely in institutional archives
options.B: Proving that complex statistical formulas were calculated correctly
options.C: Sharing completed study findings with those who can use them
options.D: Helping researchers secure permanent university promotions

explanation: You've got this! Dissemination simply means getting research out of storage and into the hands of people who can actually use it to help patients. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of an endoscope compared to a standard X-ray?

options.A: It uses radiation to map deep bone structures accurately.
options.B: It measures the chemical balance inside the stomach.
options.C: It creates a three-dimensional shadow image of organs.
options.D: It provides a direct, colored view of internal mucosal surfaces.

explanation: You've got this! Endoscopes use a tiny camera and light to let doctors see inside directly in full color, whereas X-rays only give us black-and-white shadow pictures. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is a typical feature of a benign (non-cancerous) tumor?

options.A: Surrounded by a fibrous capsule
options.B: Infiltrates surrounding normal tissues
options.C: Rapid and uncontrolled cellular division
options.D: Ability to form secondary tumors

explanation: Correct! Benign tumors usually stay put inside a neat fibrous capsule, meaning they don't invade nearby tissues or spread around. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the best way to prevent accidental needlestick injuries after giving an injection?

options.A: Carefully placing the plastic cap back onto the needle using two hands.
options.B: Dropping the uncapped needle directly into a rigid sharps box.
options.C: Leaving the used syringe on the bedside table until the end of the shift.
options.D: Breaking the needle off the syringe before throwing it in the trash.

explanation: Great job! Never try to recap a used needle—that is the number one cause of accidental pricks. Drop it straight into the safety box! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h2)

question: What is the biggest danger that causes high complications in unsafe abortions?

options.A: Early detection of pregnancy in a regulated hospital setting
options.B: The use of untrained providers and unsterile conditions
options.C: Regular monitoring by professional obstetric nurses
options.D: The prescription of standard medical abortion pills by doctors

explanation: Unsafe abortions often involve dirty tools and untrained people, which sadly leads to heavy infections and severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h3)

question: Why do public health teams create a clear 'case definition' during an outbreak?

options.A: To determine which pharmaceutical company supplies drugs
options.B: To decide clearly who is counted as having the outbreak disease
options.C: To write a legal penalty for people who refuse treatment
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of hospital supplies

explanation: You got it! A case definition gives healthcare workers clear, shared rules to correctly identify and count true cases during an outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to be extra careful when older patients take nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)?

options.A: They block the absorption of all essential vitamins in the diet
options.B: They immediately cause complete muscle paralysis in the limbs
options.C: They permanently cure degenerative disc disease within days
options.D: They carry a high risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and kidney stress

explanation: NSAIDs are great for pain, but elderly stomachs and kidneys are extra sensitive to them, risking ulcers and strain. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T24#GNS222_U1_T24_h6)

question: Why must nurses be careful when evaluating pain in older adult patients?

options.A: Older adults do not experience acute nociceptive pain.
options.B: Older adults always report pain at a much higher intensity than young adults.
options.C: Standard rating scales cannot be understood by anyone over age sixty-five.
options.D: Pain should never be assumed to be a normal, expected part of aging.

explanation: Never brush off pain just because someone is elderly. Assuming it's 'just old age' leads to missing treatable problems! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h5)

question: What does 'susceptible host' mean in the chain of infection?

options.A: A person who transmits viruses through the air
options.B: A person who is completely immune to all germs
options.C: A person whose body cannot easily fight off an invading germ
options.D: A person who acts as a permanent reservoir for bacteria

explanation: You got it! A susceptible host simply lacks the immunity or strength to stop a pathogen from causing an infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for active bleeding from an arm wound?

options.A: Elevate the arm and wait
options.B: Wash the open wound thoroughly with cold water
options.C: Apply firm, direct pressure with a clean dressing
options.D: Tie a tight tourniquet above the elbow

explanation: Direct pressure is always your go-to first step! It helps mechanical clotting do its job right away. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h5)

question: How were patients typically treated inside early asylums?

options.A: Trained in useful vocational skills
options.B: Involved in daily group therapy sessions
options.C: Given regular rest periods and nutritious meals
options.D: Chained, neglected, and viewed as public spectacles

explanation: Conditions were brutal, and facilities even charged admission fees for tourists to come and stare at the inmates. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h2)

question: What do we call inflammation of the middle layer of the eye, which includes the iris?

options.A: Keratitis
options.B: Conjunctivitis
options.C: Retinitis
options.D: Uveitis

explanation: You got it! Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea (the middle layer). It can cause a deep, aching pain and make the eyes very sensitive to light. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T4#GNS311_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is testicular torsion treated as an urgent medical emergency?

options.A: It causes an immediate permanent drop in total body testosterone
options.B: It always spreads a severe bacterial infection to the bladder
options.C: It triggers rapid enlargement of the prostate gland
options.D: It cuts off blood supply and can damage the tissue

explanation: When the spermatic cord twists, it blocks blood flow to the testicle. This is an emergency because the tissue needs oxygen fast to prevent permanent damage! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h2)

question: What is the target INR range for a standard patient taking warfarin for deep vein thrombosis?
explanation: An INR of 2.0 to 3.0 is the sweet spot for warfarin therapy—it keeps clots away without letting bleeding get out of hand. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h4)

question: What is the main functional challenge when a patient has a congenitally shortened fallopian tube?

options.A: The time window for optimal gamete interaction and transport is compressed
options.B: Progesterone production by the tubal mucosa is permanently doubled
options.C: Sperm are completely blocked from entering the peritoneal cavity
options.D: Ovulation is prevented from occurring on the affected side

explanation: A shorter tube means less time and space for the delicate timing needed between sperm meeting the egg and the egg traveling down safely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h4)

question: What is an objective in healthcare administration?

options.A: A random list of daily tasks with no fixed timeline
options.B: A legal document signed only by the hospital owner
options.C: A specific and measurable target for planning and operations
options.D: A punishment system for healthcare workers who make mistakes

explanation: Think of an objective as your clear target. In nursing administration, having specific, measurable goals helps everyone know what work to focus on each day. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the medical term when individual cells grow larger in size?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Think 'hyper' (more/bigger) and 'trophy' (growth). Hypertrophy means the cells are getting bigger, not multiplying! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h4)

question: What physical event causes a sudden rise in the newborn's systemic blood pressure?

options.A: Clamping of the umbilical cord
options.B: The baby crying for the first time
options.C: Closure of the foramen ovale
options.D: Contraction of the ductus arteriosus

explanation: Cutting the cord removes the low-resistance placenta, which sharply increases resistance and pressure in the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: What mental health challenge do rehabilitation psychologists most commonly help patients work through?

options.A: Physical balance and dizziness
options.B: Nutritional deficits and tube-feeding routines
options.C: Managing acute surgical site pain
options.D: Coping with a sudden disability and grief

explanation: A life-altering illness or injury brings deep emotional pain. Rehab psychologists help patients process these feelings and adapt to their new reality. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h7)

question: What is the main job of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in males?

options.A: Supporting sperm production in the Sertoli cells
options.B: Producing secondary sex characteristics in muscle
options.C: Triggering the release of gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: Controlling the contraction of the prostate gland

explanation: FSH works directly on the Sertoli cells in the testes to help nourish and build healthy sperm cells. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h1)

question: A community health nurse notices several children from different families coming in with the exact same pesticide poisoning signs. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Advise the local schools to close down all science laboratories
options.B: Treat the children and assume it is an isolated domestic accident
options.C: Wait until the end of the year to write a formal summary report
options.D: Report the cluster to public health authorities for investigation

explanation: You've got it! When multiple cases point to a shared source, alerting public health authorities right away helps track down the cause and protect the whole neighborhood. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h7)

question: A patient struggles to understand a complicated medication schedule with four different drugs. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to double the morning dose instead
options.B: Scold the patient for being careless with prescriptions
options.C: Stop all the medications until the patient feels better
options.D: Work with the doctor to simplify the dosing schedule

explanation: Simplifying complex regimens reduces confusion and makes it much easier for the patient to follow the treatment plan. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h7)

question: What actually happens when there is 'sampling bias' in research?

options.A: An error caused by using a broken weighing scale in the clinic
options.B: The refusal of patients to answer personal questions in a survey
options.C: A systematic flaw that favors certain individuals over others in selection
options.D: The natural mathematical difference between a sample and a population

explanation: Spot on! Sampling bias means your selection method accidentally gives some people a better chance of being picked than others, skewing your results. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h6)

question: Which communication channel works best for reaching people in remote rural areas in their own language?

options.A: Radio broadcasts
options.B: Academic journals
options.C: Official letters
options.D: Social media posts

explanation: Radio is a powerful tool in Nigeria, reaching deep into rural communities where smartphones and internet might not be available. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h5)

question: In the famous ABCDE emergency checklist, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Behavior
options.B: Bleeding
options.C: Breathing
options.D: Bedside

explanation: Easy peasy! After checking the Airway (A), the next urgent priority is checking Breathing (B) to make sure oxygen is flowing. [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why does a lower pH number mean higher acidity?

options.A: A lower number shows that bicarbonate levels have increased
options.B: A lower number indicates fewer metabolic wastes in the plasma
options.C: A lower number represents a complete lack of dissolved gases
options.D: A lower number means a higher amount of free hydrogen ions

explanation: Think of it this way: the more free hydrogen ions pile up, the more acidic the fluid becomes, and the lower the pH number drops. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h1)

question: Generally speaking, what is the minimum acceptable hourly urine output for an adult?

options.A: 5.0 mL/kg/hour
options.B: 0.5 mL/kg/hour
options.C: 2.0 mL/kg/hour
options.D: 10.0 mL/kg/hour

explanation: Keep 0.5 mL/kg/hour in mind! Anything less than this tells you the kidneys aren't getting enough blood flow. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which group requires a higher proportion of protein and energy relative to body weight?

options.A: Sedentary older adults
options.B: Patients with chronic joint pain
options.C: Healthy middle-aged men
options.D: Infants and growing children

explanation: Rapid growth and cellular multiplication during childhood demand a high intake of building blocks like protein. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h6)

question: What is the main job of a flight nurse?

options.A: Repairing aircraft engines and systems
options.B: Piloting emergency medical helicopters
options.C: Managing hospital intensive care units
options.D: Providing medical care during aircraft transport

explanation: You've got this! Flight nurses specialize in looking after patients and giving continuous medical care while flying in an aircraft. Simple and vital! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T14#GNS321_U2_T14_h1)

question: At what point in their journey can a cancer patient start receiving palliative care?

options.A: When the patient's life expectancy drops below two weeks
options.B: Once the patient is admitted to a dedicated hospice facility
options.C: At the time of diagnosis, alongside active curative treatments
options.D: Only after all forms of chemotherapy and radiation have failed

explanation: Brilliant! Palliative care isn't just for end-of-life; it can—and should—start right from diagnosis to help manage symptoms while active treatment happens. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h8)

question: What happens if a research question is unclear or confusing?

options.A: Readers and data collectors will not know what is actually being measured
options.B: The institutional review board will automatically approve it
options.C: The study will take fewer days to complete
options.D: Data analysis becomes completely unnecessary

explanation: Clarity is key. If your question is confusing, anyone helping you collect data will be lost, leading to messy results that don't make sense. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h2)

question: A rural village uses its own communal labor and local materials to build a shade structure for an immunization clinic. Which objective does this best demonstrate?

options.A: Strict political control
options.B: Individual clinical diagnosis
options.C: External donor dependency
options.D: Resource mobilisation

explanation: Using local labour and materials to support a health project is a clear example of resource mobilisation from within the community. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is double-checking the patient's ID band considered the absolute most important rule before a blood transfusion?

options.A: It ensures the hospital billing department charges the correct patient
options.B: It guarantees the blood donor receives proper compensation
options.C: It prevents clerical errors that can cause fatal incompatible reactions
options.D: It speeds up the time it takes to deliver blood from the lab

explanation: Spotting identity mistakes saves lives! Giving blood to the wrong person is a major cause of dangerous reactions, making this check vital. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h1)

question: Why do we regularly check liver function and platelet counts for a mum with severe preeclampsia?

options.A: To calculate her exact delivery date
options.B: To check for liver stress and HELLP syndrome
options.C: To check if the baby can breathe on its own
options.D: To find out the sex of the baby

explanation: Severe preeclampsia can sneak up on the liver and use up clotting cells (platelets). Watching these lab results helps us catch dangerous changes early! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h4)

question: Which communication channel is best suited for building deep trust and allowing immediate feedback with a patient?

options.A: A prerecorded radio jingle
options.B: Interpersonal communication
options.C: A national television advertisement
options.D: A billboard on a major highway

explanation: Nothing beats face-to-face talk! Interpersonal communication lets you clear doubts, answer questions directly, and build wonderful rapport with your patients. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h4)

question: How does better nutrition quietly boost a patient's overall quality of life?

options.A: By increasing their financial income through savings
options.B: By ensuring they never experience physical pain again
options.C: By giving them the energy to enjoy daily activities and hobbies
options.D: By making them sleep for twelve hours every night

explanation: Exactly! When chronic fatigue fades away, patients can finally get back to enjoying their daily walks, family gatherings, and favorite hobbies. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h6)

question: What is the main goal of grouping drugs into pharmacological classes?

options.A: To determine the exact retail cost of prescription drugs
options.B: To establish the legal expiration date for various drug classes
options.C: To identify which pharmaceutical company manufactured the medicine
options.D: To group medications based on their mechanism and physiological effects

explanation: Grouping drugs by how they work in the body helps you easily predict their actions and safety profiles without memorizing every single pill! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h1)

question: During normal digestion, what is the main job of the large intestine?

options.A: Breaking down complex proteins into simple amino acids
options.B: Producing bile acids needed for fat digestion
options.C: Absorbing water and electrolytes from waste material
options.D: Secreting large amounts of digestive enzymes into chyme

explanation: Great job! As food waste travels through the colon, the large intestine's primary task is to pull water and minerals back into the body. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why is caring for someone with Pick's disease often so emotionally draining for families?

options.A: The disease progresses much faster than any other form of dementia.
options.B: Patients require constant surgical procedures throughout the illness.
options.C: Family members are legally required to pay for all hospital care.
options.D: The loss of personality and social filter can feel emotionally rejecting.

explanation: It hurts deeply when a loved one changes personality, loses their warmth, or acts out of character. Families need plenty of empathy and support from nurses to cope with this grief. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h7)

question: When would a doctor choose a balloon dilator instead of a solid bougie?

options.A: When radial, controlled pressure is needed under direct visualization
options.B: When the patient is completely unconscious in the emergency room
options.C: When the stricture requires heavy metal weight to force it open
options.D: When direct tactile feedback through the hands is the only goal

explanation: Balloon dilators use air or fluid to expand outward evenly in all directions, and doctors usually place them using an endoscope so they can see what they're doing. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h2)

question: A patient with hearing loss is struggling to catch your discharge instructions. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask a family member to take over all patient care responsibilities
options.B: Face the patient directly and speak in a clear, moderate tone
options.C: Shout loudly from across the room so they can hear better
options.D: Stop talking and write everything down in complex medical terms

question: Which of these is NOT a common financial or social barrier to healthcare access in Nigeria?

options.A: High out-of-pocket expenses for routine medications and blood tests

options.C: Free and unlimited universal healthcare coverage for all citizens
options.D: Long travel distances from rural villages to tertiary teaching hospitals

question: What is the main job of wearable health devices in clinical care?

options.A: To deliver oral medications automatically to the patient
options.B: To diagnose complex surgical diseases without a doctor
options.C: To track and transmit health-related data continuously
options.D: To replace traditional laboratory blood testing completely

explanation: Wearables are great because they keep an eye on patient vitals between clinic visits. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why do we strongly advise against using both hands to recap a needle?

options.D: It takes too much time during an emergency

question: What is the main cause of painful breast engorgement in the first few days after giving birth?

options.A: Bacterial infection spreading through the lactiferous ducts
options.B: Blockage of the nipple pores by dried colostrum
options.C: A sudden drop in maternal oxytocin during feedings
options.D: Vascular congestion and the initial rush of milk coming in

question: How did Nigerian mothers traditionally space their children before modern contraceptives arrived?

options.A: Daily ingestion of synthetic hormone pills
options.B: Intrauterine copper device insertion
options.C: Surgical tubal ligation procedures
options.D: Prolonged breastfeeding and postpartum abstinence

explanation: Traditional Nigerian societies used natural, reliable spacing methods like extended breastfeeding and resting from sex after childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h5)

question: A public health nurse hands out mosquito nets to prevent malaria. Which part of the epidemiological triad is this mainly targeting?

options.A: Incubation period
options.B: Agent
options.C: Host genetics
options.D: Environment

explanation: Spot on! Mosquito nets create a physical block between you and the environmental vector, modifying the surrounding environment where disease transmission happens. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h3)

question: What are the two major muscle problems seen in a patient with achalasia?

options.A: Premature contraction of the diaphragm and paralysis of the phrenic nerve
options.B: Weakness of the upper sphincter and rapid food transit into the duodenum
options.C: Constant spasm of the upper sphincter and excessive stomach acid production
options.D: Failure of the lower sphincter to relax and lack of normal peristalsis

question: What do deep, wide Q waves usually point to on an ECG?

options.A: Myocardial infarction and tissue necrosis
options.B: Temporary lack of oxygen called ischemia
options.C: Atrial enlargement from high blood pressure
options.D: Normal athletic heart enlargement

question: Why must a nurse check a patient's medication list before starting them on calcium supplements?

options.A: Calcium completely neutralizes the effects of all known blood pressure medications.

options.C: Calcium increases the rate at which the kidneys excrete water-soluble drugs.
options.D: Calcium can bind to certain antibiotics in the gut and stop them from working.

explanation: Spot on! Calcium binds with certain drugs (like tetracyclines) in the stomach, forming a combo your body can't absorb. Always check for drug interactions! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h8)

question: Which brain chemical is severely lacking in Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Serotonin

explanation: Parkinson's disease specifically results from the death of neurons that produce dopamine in a part of the midbrain called the substantia nigra. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h3)

question: What makes an infant's upper airway much easier to block compared to an adult's?

options.C: Complete rigidity of the upper airway cartilage
options.D: An absence of mucus glands in the pharynx

question: Why is watching closely for signs of infection so important for patients on chemotherapy?

options.A: Patients are unable to take oral fluids during chemotherapy treatment

options.C: Chemotherapy lowers the white blood cell count, making the body vulnerable to pathogens
options.D: Ovarian tumors produce bacteria that multiply rapidly in the bloodstream

explanation: Brilliant! Chemotherapy temporarily slows down bone marrow function, leaving the patient with fewer white blood cells to fight off germs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h8)

question: Why is the living will movement considered a shift away from medical paternalism?

options.A: Because nurses take over the legal responsibilities of physicians
options.B: Because patients now direct their care instead of doctors making every choice
options.C: Because hospitals no longer require doctors to write treatment orders
options.D: Because family members now pay all medical bills directly

explanation: Traditional medical paternalism meant doctors decided everything. Living wills put the decision-making power back into the hands of the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which screening tool is most commonly used to check for perinatal depression and anxiety?

options.A: Glasgow coma scale assessment
options.B: Apgar newborn scoring system
options.C: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale
options.D: Braden skin breakdown scale

explanation: Brilliant! The EPDS is the standard questionnaire used worldwide to help detect mood changes in new and expectant mums. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T004#GNS226_U2_T004_h7)

question: What does the term intersectionality describe in patient care?

options.A: The physical meeting point where blood vessels cross in the body
options.B: The exact moment when a patient transitions from childhood to adulthood
options.C: How multiple social identities overlap to shape unique life experiences
options.D: How biological sex interacts strictly with inherited genetic diseases

explanation: Intersectionality highlights that factors like race, gender, and class combine to influence a person's unique health realities and challenges. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h5)

question: In Nigeria, which season is historically tied to outbreaks of meningococcal meningitis?

options.A: The coastal harvest season
options.B: The heavy rainy season
options.C: The dry harmattan season
options.D: The humid summer solstice

explanation: Dry harmattan winds dry out and irritate the lining of our noses and throats, making it super easy for meningitis bacteria to slip past our defenses and cause outbreaks in our communities. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T17#GNS222_U3_T17_h8)

question: Why do we give emergency epinephrine into the thigh muscle instead of the arm?

options.A: The drug is absorbed much faster into the bloodstream from the thigh
options.B: The skin on the thigh feels less pain
options.C: Arm muscles are too small for emergency drugs
options.D: It stops the patient from seeing the needle

explanation: The vastus lateralis muscle in the thigh has great blood flow, helping the epinephrine get to work as fast as possible when every second counts. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h7)

question: How does low socioeconomic status typically impact a patient's long-term adaptation to a chronic illness?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for professional nursing care
options.B: It forces the body to stop experiencing the alarm stage of stress
options.C: It automatically guarantees a faster psychological recovery
options.D: It can limit access to essential medications and healthy nutrition

explanation: Financial hardship restricts access to necessary health resources, making sustained disease management and adaptation significantly harder. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do we usually avoid estrogen-containing pills for mothers who are breastfeeding?

options.A: They can significantly reduce the breast milk supply
options.B: They transfer directly into breast milk as a heavy poison
options.C: They stimulate excessive and painful uterine contractions
options.D: They always cause immediate cessation of all lochia

explanation: Estrogen can lower milk volume. That is why progestin-only options or non-hormonal methods are much safer choices for nursing mums early on. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h2)

question: What should you do right after the AED delivers a shock?

options.A: Resume chest compressions immediately.
options.B: Wait for the doctor to arrive and give orders.
options.C: Check for a carotid pulse for ten seconds.
options.D: Remove the electrode pads from the chest.

question: A nurse is teaching a patient how to collect a sputum sample for testing. Which instruction is best?

options.A: Collect clear saliva immediately after eating a heavy meal
options.B: Rinse the mouth thoroughly with strong antiseptic mouthwash before coughing
options.C: Store the collected container in the domestic refrigerator overnight
options.D: Provide a deep cough sample first thing in the morning

explanation: Brilliant! Early morning deep-cough samples are best because secretions and parasite eggs pool up overnight, making them easier to catch. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h5)

question: A patient touches a hot stove and quickly pulls their hand away. Which receptors flagged this danger?

options.A: Proprioceptors and mechanoreceptors
options.B: Baroreceptors and chemoreceptors
options.C: Photoreceptors and osmoreceptors
options.D: Thermoreceptors and nociceptors

explanation: Brilliant! Thermoreceptors felt the intense heat, and nociceptors screamed 'ouch!'—triggering that fast reflex to protect the hand. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h3)

question: What kind of infectious agent causes Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)?

options.A: A slow-acting bacterial spore

options.C: A parasitic protozoan in brain tissue
options.D: A mutant strand of DNA virus

question: How is being 'hard of hearing' different from profound deafness?

options.A: Hard of hearing always requires immediate surgical intervention
options.B: Hard of hearing individuals retain some residual hearing capacity
options.C: Deafness is always caused by an infection in the outer ear
options.D: Deaf individuals can still understand whispered conversations easily

explanation: Patients who are hard of hearing still have some hearing left (residual hearing). This means devices like hearing aids can help them a lot! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T14#GNS324_U4_T14_h1)

question: A confused patient arrives at the emergency department with suspected drug ingestion. What quick bedside check must a nurse perform right away?

options.A: Checking blood glucose level
options.B: Measuring abdominal girth
options.C: Testing deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Checking visual acuity

question: What is the main job of the ductus arteriosus?

options.C: It connects the umbilical cord directly to the placenta
options.D: It directs blood from the pulmonary artery into the aorta

question: Where do the coronary arteries get their blood supply from?

question: What should a nurse tell a patient taking liquid iron syrup to prevent staining their teeth?

question: Why do researchers weigh risks and benefits before starting a study?

question: A nurse believes a new wound dressing heals ulcers faster. What represents the alternative hypothesis?

question: Which set of lab tests is primarily ordered to check how well the thyroid gland is working?

question: Why do people with the same genetic background sometimes have different cancer risks?

question: A woman in early labor has an Hb result of 8.5 g/dL. What category does this fall into?

question: According to the Ann Arbor staging system, what defines Stage III lymphoma?

question: What happens during drug distribution in the body?

question: Which group is most likely covered by strict mandatory reporting laws that require action even without adult consent?

question: Why might a patient experience a fast heartbeat (tachycardia) and hand tremors after using a rescue inhaler?

question: Which of these is an example of using an endoscope for treatment (therapeutic)?

question: Which of these materials must always be disposed of through incineration?

question: A nursing mum in the clinic needs affordable protein options available in local Nigerian markets. What should you suggest?

options.D: Beans, crayfish, and lean fish

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

question: What is the very first step a nurse must take when planning a community health program?

question: What is the primary purpose of directing in nursing management?

question: What is the main goal of good nutrition in Primary Health Care (PHC)?

question: What is the name of the thick, yellowish fluid the breasts produce in the later stages of pregnancy?

question: Why do poorly ventilated and overcrowded rooms make the spread of TB worse?

question: What is the classic leg pain sign that happens when walking if someone has Peripheral Artery Disease?

question: What is orthostatic hypotension?

question: A community located twenty kilometers from the nearest health post has very low immunization rates due to bad roads. What is the most effective intervention?

question: What is the main goal of Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)?

options.A: To suppress viral replication and reduce the viral load to undetectable levels

options.D: To cure advanced stages of AIDS within two weeks of treatment

question: How has flight nursing changed from the old days to modern times?

question: Which major nerve provides 'rest-and-digest' signals to speed up activity throughout the GI tract?

question: A patient comes in complaining of a heavy, squeezing chest pressure spreading to their jaw while doing chores. What does this classic sign point to?

question: What is the primary focus of preventive nursing in musculoskeletal health?

question: In the emergency ABCDE assessment check, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

question: If a hospital team wants to figure out the clinical factors behind a recent rise in maternal deaths at their facility, what process should they join?

options.D: Maternal Death Surveillance and Response (MDSR) audits

question: Why do regular smokers need to smoke more over time to feel the same buzz?

question: Which supportive procedure is commonly used to give the bowel a rest during an acute GI crisis?

options.C: Daily strenuous exercise
options.D: High-fiber meal planning

explanation: Spot on! An NG tube suctions out stomach contents and gas, which lets the bowel rest and prevents further pressure or vomiting. You are building up great practical knowledge! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h8)

question: Which of these is a FALSE statement about how HIV spreads that nurses should correct in the community?

options.A: HIV can pass from a mother to her child during breastfeeding
options.B: HIV is easily spread through sharing eating utensils and drinking glasses
options.C: HIV is spread through direct contact with infected blood
options.D: HIV is transmitted through unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected partner

explanation: Correct! Sharing spoons or cups does not spread HIV because the virus dies quickly outside the body and isn't passed through casual saliva. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h7)

question: What is the nurse's main role when working alongside local faith-based support systems?

options.A: Supervising the theological training of local pastors and priests
options.B: Replacing traditional medical treatments with purely spiritual rituals
options.C: Coordinating care to bridge clinical needs with community spiritual resources
options.D: Regulating the financial donations given to religious organizations

explanation: As nurses, we connect everyday hospital or clinic care with the community support systems that help patients thrive as whole human beings. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for improving PTA effectiveness in school health? (Look for the exception)

options.A: Ensuring transparent accounting of all funds raised for projects
options.B: Focusing meetings solely on demanding financial levies without explanations
options.C: Inviting community health nurses to give health talks during meetings
options.D: Partnering with local health centers for regular student screenings

explanation: Focusing only on money without engaging parents in health education or being transparent causes apathy and drives parents away. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h7)

question: How should a nurse address the psychological needs of a patient preparing for fistula repair?

options.A: Focus only on physical care because emotional feelings do not affect healing
options.B: Tell the patient that her condition is very rare and difficult to cure
options.C: Provide compassionate, non-judgmental support and explain all procedures clearly
options.D: Avoid talking about the condition to prevent embarrassing the patient

explanation: Patients suffer from heavy emotional distress and isolation, making empathetic communication and reassurance a vital part of nursing care. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: Which of the following is considered an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?

options.A: Driving a car to work
options.B: Bathing and dressing
options.C: Cooking complex meals
options.D: Balancing a bank account

explanation: ADLs are basic self-care tasks required for daily living, including bathing, dressing, eating, and toileting. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h3)

question: Why is a nasogastric (NG) tube usually inserted for a patient with a small bowel obstruction?

options.A: To measure daily urine output accurately in dehydrated patients
options.B: To decompress the stomach and remove accumulated fluid and gas
options.C: To administer oral antibiotics without irritating the stomach lining
options.D: To deliver high-calorie liquid meals directly into the small intestine

explanation: The NG tube acts like a gentle vacuum, sucking out trapped air and fluid to relieve pressure, nausea, and vomiting. Well done! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is a major consequence when health workers judge teenagers seeking reproductive advice?

options.A: Adolescents immediately change their behavior and practice strict abstinence
options.B: Young people report the healthcare workers to international health bodies
options.C: Teenagers stop seeking professional help and turn to unsafe alternatives
options.D: Parents take over the health education role completely at home

explanation: Stigma and judgmental attitudes drive vulnerable youths away from clinics, leading to hidden risks like unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: What should you do if a patient pushes out a suppository right after you insert it?

options.A: Inspect the stool, check the status, and consult the prescriber for a repeat dose
options.B: Immediately force a second suppository into the rectum without checking
options.C: Assume the full dose was already absorbed and document successful administration
options.D: Scold the patient for failing to hold the medication inside the bowel

explanation: If it comes out whole before melting, the dose is lost, and you must check with the prescriber before trying again. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why might a doctor order a sigmoidoscopy instead of a full colonoscopy for a patient with lower left belly pain and bright red bleeding?

options.A: It needs general anesthesia and a long hospital stay.
options.B: It replaces all future bowel tests completely.
options.C: It targets the lower third of the colon where these symptoms usually start.
options.D: It shows a clear view of the entire stomach and gut.

explanation: Great thinking! When issues are right down in the lower bowel, a sigmoidoscopy is a quick, targeted way to check things out without needing a full-length scope. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h1)

question: When can a patient safely start a new method of contraception after a medical abortion?

options.A: Only after waiting six full months
options.B: After the next normal menstrual period
options.C: Immediately on the same day
options.D: Strictly after a surgical checkup

explanation: Correct! Fertility can return almost immediately, so patients can start new birth control methods like pills or implants on the exact same day they take the abortion medications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h7)
